findings.title: OAuth integration with per-user authorization flow
findings.detail: Each customer authorizes the integration through the OAuth flow; the access token is tied to that user and used for subsequent API requests. Notion's page picker limits access to pages the user selects.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations/workspaces connect and each customer authorizes the app.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
**Step 5** Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.
**Step 3** The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.

findings.title: Read content capability for shared pages
findings.detail: The Read content capability lets a connection read existing content, including retrieving pages and block children; without it calls return 403. Shared pages are only accessible when the user selected them in the page picker.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading page titles and content through the API.

evidence.quote: * **Read content**: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
### Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or property, or missing access to the page, returns `404`.
> > This endpoint requires a connection to have read content capabilities. Attempting to call this API without read content capabilities will return an HTTP response with a 403 status

findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connecting to the app.

findings.title: Page retrieval endpoints for titles and content
findings.detail: Retrieve a page returns the page with title property; retrieve block children returns page content with pagination via next_cursor and has_more. Retrieve page as markdown can return truncated content with unknown_block_ids that must be re-fetched.

steps.title: Read shared page and resolve its title property
steps.detail: Retrieve the customer-shared page. Find the property whose type is title by scanning properties.*.type == "title" (the key is not fixed; do not assume properties.title). Join the title[].plain_text segments in array order to form the title. Use filter_properties only if it does not omit the title-type property. The page_id is user-provided and was shared during consent. Boundary check: request a page the customer did not share and confirm a 404 with no content returned.
steps.doneWhen: The title is read from the property where type is title, all plain_text segments are joined in order, and an unshared page returns 404.

steps.title: Read first-level block children with pagination
steps.detail: List first-level children of the page with page_size 100. For each text-bearing block, join every rich_text[].plain_text segment in array order. Continue with next_cursor while has_more is true. For every returned block with has_children true, repeat this paginated block-children call using that block's results[].id until has_more is false, recursing through nested children. Two pages alone are not a complete listing. Boundary check: confirm only GET block-children requests are logged and no write request is made.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are read until has_more is false at every level, each child block with has_children true is fetched with its own paginated calls, and rich_text segments are joined in full.

steps.detail: Repeat the block-children request for the same block_id with start_cursor set to next_cursor from the prior response and page_size 100, until has_more is false.
